q: 1. For excavating solid rocks, the most suitable equipment?
explain: The power shovel provides the highest breakout force, making it the best choice for digging hard or blasted rock.

q: 2. The size of a power shovel is indicated by the size of ............
explain: Power shovels are rated by the capacity (volume) of their 'dipper' or bucket.

q: 3. Which one of the following does not from a part of Derrick crane?
explain: A Derrick crane consists of a mast, a boom (incorrectly spelled 'book' in text), and guy wires. A jack is a separate lifting tool.

q: 4. Which one of the following does not fall under the category hoisting equipment?
explain: A Dragline is excavating equipment. While it has hoisting cables, its primary function is excavation, not dedicated lifting like a hoist or jack.

q: 5. Which of the following conveyor is never used?
explain: All the listed types (Spiral, Roller, and Screw) are standard conveyors used in various industrial and construction material handling applications.

q: 6. A canal is trimmed on its side and bottom by ............
explain: Mechanical trimmers are specialized machines used to precisely finish the slopes and beds of canals before lining.

q: 7. The direct cost of a project with respect normal time is ............
explain: At normal time, the project is executed using the most efficient methods and standard resources, resulting in the lowest possible direct cost.

q: 8. Economic saving of time result by crashing ............
explain: To reduce project duration economically, we always crash the activity on the critical path that has the lowest cost slope (the cheapest to compress).

q: 9. The process of incorporating changes and rescheduling or preplanning is called ............
explain: Updating is the process of re-evaluating the project network periodically to account for actual progress and making necessary adjustments to future schedules.

q: 10. Which of the following is the correct from of representation of an event?
explain: In a network diagram, an event (a point in time marking the start or end of an activity) is standardly represented by a circle or a node.

q: 11. Which of the following is not related to cost slope?
explain: Cost slope is calculated using (Crash Cost - Normal Cost) / (Normal Time - Crash Time). Slack is a time-related buffer for events and is not part of the cost slope formula.

q: 12. Use of dummies is required for ............
explain: Dummy activities consume zero time and resources; they are used solely to maintain the correct logic and dependencies between activities in a network.

q: 13. Latest finish time in C.P.M. technique is indicated by a ............
explain: According to the provided answer key (and common CPM chart standards), the rectangle is used to represent the boundary times like Latest Finish.

q: 14. The essential condition for the decompression of an activity is that ............
options: the project time should change due to decompression
after decompression, the time of an activity invariably exceeds its normal time
an activity could be decompressed to the maximum extent of its normal time
explain: Decompression is the reverse of crashing. You can only expand an activity's duration back to its original 'Normal Time' but not beyond it.

q: 15. Dummy activities are used to ............
explain: Dummies are structural tools in a network diagram used to show relationships (logic) when two activities share the same start and end nodes.

q: 16. Which of the following are the guidelines for the construction of a network diagram?
options: each activity is represented by one only arrow in the network
dangling must be avoided in a network diagram
dummy activity consumes no time or resource
explain: These are fundamental rules: unique arrows per activity, avoiding loose ends (dangling), and utilizing zero-duration dummies for logic.

q: 17. Due to omission of any part of a project, the duration of project will ............
explain: Removing a scope of work (omission) generally reduces the total amount of work to be done, thereby decreasing the project duration.

q: 18. Due to omission of any part of a project, the cost of project will ............
explain: If a portion of the project is removed, the direct costs associated with those materials and labor are subtracted from the total project cost.

q: 19. Sensitivity analysis is a study of .............
options: change in output due to change in input
economics of cost and benefits of the project
explain: Sensitivity analysis determines how different values of an independent variable (input) affect a particular dependent variable (output) under a given set of assumptions.

q: 20. In the time-cost optimisation, using C.P.M. method for network analysis, the crashing of the activities along the critical path is done starting with the activity having .............
explain: To minimize the increase in project cost while shortening the duration, activities on the critical path with the lowest cost slope (least expensive to crash) are prioritized.

q: 21. Preliminary project report for a road project must contain .............
options: the detailed estimated cost based on detailed design
the several alternatives of the project that have been considered
the soil survey, traffic survey, concept design and approximate cost
the contract documents for inviting tenders
explain: A preliminary report focuses on feasibility and basic data like soil types, traffic volume, and rough cost estimates before moving to detailed design.

options: a large dam constructed across a river for a single or multi-purpose
any job involving many people and large money
a work of major importance involving huge men and material
an organised team work to achieve a set task within the time limit
explain: A project is defined by its temporary nature (time limit) and its specific goal-oriented organization.

q: 23. An activity is .............
options: an element of work entailed in the project
the movement of heavy vehicles from one place to another
the beginning or the end of a specified job
the progress of work up to certain limit
explain: In network analysis, an activity is a specific task or element of work that consumes time and resources.

q: 24. The pictorial representation of activities and events of a project is known as the .............
explain: A project network is a graphical flow diagram showing the sequence of activities and their interdependencies.

q: 25. The flow of time in a net work is generally .............
explain: Standard network conventions dictate that the project timeline progresses from left (start) to right (finish).

q: 26. Bar chart is also known as .............
explain: Bar charts used in project management were developed by Henry Gantt and are widely referred to as Gantt charts.

q: 27. Systematic reporting of work progress is the main objective of .............
explain: A flow process chart is used to track the sequence of all operations, transportations, inspections, and delays in a process to report and analyze progress.

q: 28. P.E.R.T. technique of network analysis is mainly useful for .............
explain: PERT is a probabilistic technique designed for projects with high uncertainty, such as R&D, where activity times aren't precisely known.

q: 29. Which of the following is not a P.E.R.T. event?
explain: 'Class is being attended' is an ongoing process (activity), not a specific point in time (event).

q: 30. In P.E.R.T. analysis, the time estimates of activities and probability of their occurrence follow .............
explain: PERT assumes activity durations follow a Beta distribution to account for skewness in optimistic/pessimistic times.

q: 31. For excavating utility trenches with precise control of depth, the excavation equipment used is .............
explain: A backhoe (or hoe) is the most effective for trenching because it works below its own track level with high precision.

q: 32. Free float is mainly used to .............
options: identify the activities which can be delayed without affecting the total float of succeeding activity
identify the activities, which can be delayed without affecting the start of succeeding activity
identify the activities which can be delayed without affecting the total of either the preceding of succeeding activities
explain: Free float is the amount of time an activity can be delayed without delaying the Earliest Start (ES) of any immediate successor.

q: 33. A milestone chart .............
options: shows the inter dependence of various jobs
shows the events in chronological, but in a logical sequence
explain: Milestone charts focus on key project events (milestones) chronologically, though they don't show interdependencies as well as networks.

q: 34. Time estimated time required to complete an activity is termed as .............
explain: Duration is the standard term for the time spent on performing an activity.

q: 35. The variance of the P.E.R.T. critical path is equal to .............
options: sum of variance of activities lying on critical path
maximum of sum of variance upto end event
minimum of sum of variances upto end event
explain: According to the central limit theorem, the variance of the whole path is the sum of the variances of the individual activities on that path.

q: 36. In case of burst event the latest permissible occurrence time is .............
options: maximum of LSTs of the bursting activities
maximum of ESTs of the bursting activities
minimum of LSTs of the bursting activities
minimum of ESTs of the bursting activities
explain: When moving backward through a network (backward pass), the TL (Latest Time) of a burst node is the minimum of the Latest Start Times of all outgoing activities.

q: 37. There are three parallel paths in part of a network between a bursting node and the next merging node with only one activity in each path. The minimum number of dummy arrows needed will be .............
explain: To keep the identity of activities unique (since they share the same start and end nodes), 2 dummies are required for 3 parallel activities.

q: 38. Whenever an activity has zero total float, then .............
options: free float must be zero but independent float need not be zero
independent float must be zero but free float need not be zero
free float and independent float both must be zero
free float and independent float both need not be zero
explain: Since Independent Float ≤ Free Float ≤ Total Float, if Total Float is zero, the others must also be zero (assuming non-negative values).

q: 39. Total float for any activity is defined as the difference between .............
options: its latest finish time and earliest start time for its successor activity
its latest starts time and earliest start time
its latest start time and earliest finish time
its earliest finish time and earliest start time for its successor activity
explain: Total Float = Latest Start Time - Earliest Start Time (or LFT - EFT).

q: 40. Which one of the following is associated with a critical activity in a A-O-A network?
explain: By definition, a critical activity is one that has zero float, meaning any delay in it will delay the entire project.

q: 41. Selected the incorrect statements ..............
options: a critical path always begins at the very first event
a critical path always terminates at the last event
critical activities control the project duration
critical activity is the one for which free float is zero
explain: A critical activity is defined by having a Total Float of zero. While its free float will also be zero, the primary defining characteristic used in network analysis is the zero total float.

q: 42. Crash project duration is obtained by summing the ..............
options: normal durations for all the activities
crash durations for all the activities along the critical path obtained by taking into account the normal duration for the activities
crash durations for all the activities along the critical path obtained by taking into account the crash duration for all the activities
explain: The crash project duration is the shortest possible time to complete the project, calculated by summing the crash durations of activities along the path that remains critical when all activities are crashed.

options: time optimisation is given prime importance
cost optimisation is given prime importance
cost is directly proportional to time
explain: CPM is a deterministic model often used in construction where cost-time trade-offs (crashing) are a primary focus to find the optimum project cost.

q: 44. Indirect cost of the project ..............
options: decrease up to optimum duration and then increase with duration
explain: Indirect costs (overhead, administration, insurance) are time-dependent; the longer the project continues, the higher the total indirect cost.

q: 45. Work study comprises ..............
explain: Work study is a generic term for those techniques, particularly method study and work measurement, which are used in the examination of human work.

q: 46. Gnatt chart indicates ..............
options: balance of work to be done
comparison of actual progress with the scheduled progress
explain: Gantt charts are primarily used for scheduling and monitoring, allowing managers to see actual progress bars plotted against the original planned bars.

q: 47. The weakness in bar chart is ..............
options: uncertainty in duration for various activities
the sequence of activities is not very clear
explain: Bar charts struggle to show complex interdependencies between activities, do not account for uncertainty well, and can become cluttered for large projects.

q: 48. The interrelationship between the functional elements of a programme is achieve through ..............
explain: A Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) hierarchically organizes the project into functional elements, showing how sub-tasks relate to the overall project scope.

q: 49. The probability factor Z in P.E.R.T. is given by ..............
options: scheduled time - earliest expected time / standard deviation
scheduled time - latest allowable time / variance
latest allowable time - scheduled time / standard deviation
explain: The Z-score formula in PERT is (Ts - Te) / S, where Ts is the target/scheduled time and Te is the expected completion time.

q: 50. Float may be defined as the difference between ..............
options: latest start time and the earliest start time
latest finish time and the earliest finish time
time available and the time required to complete the activity
explain: Total Float can be calculated as LST-EST or LFT-EFT, and it essentially represents the excess time available for an activity.
